failure_analysis.what_failed: The detector is built on a *ratio* of recent-to-baseline pump effort (median of second half of the 50-sample window vs median of first half) plus an error floor. A tank leak drives its level loop to the 12 V pump limit and holds it there. Once both halves of the window are saturated the ratio collapses back to ~1.0, far below the 1.8 threshold, so the flag stays low for the whole leak even though the loop is at full drive. The traces show this exactly: tank1_leak flags nothing while effort1 sits at 12.0 V from t=170 s to t=410 s (251 missed seconds), and both_leaks misses 199+198 seconds. The detector is therefore most blind precisely when the fault is worst (severity is anti-correlated with the ratio). A second bug of the same family: after the leak clears the saturated loop keeps refilling the tank at high drive for another ~30-40 s, so an effort-only test would over-flag there too - the ratio test accidentally avoids that, but only because it is broken. Because the flag never fires, the setpoint logic never engages (IAE stays at the unmanaged value 112-142), so this is a pure detection-logic failure, not a tuning problem.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Replace the ratio test with an absolute 'loop is saturated' test on pump effort, which is the only signal that separates fault from no-fault on this plant: healthy no-fault maxima are 10.59 V (tank1 loop) and 9.26 V (tank2 loop) against a 12 V pump limit, and any outlet leak >=~1.1x forces the corresponding loop into (or near) saturation. Do not gate on tracking error, because a mild leak can be held at the setpoint with ~0 error while the drive sits at 11-12 V. Add a recovery gate (level rising >0.012 m and/or error falling >0.02 over the last 10 s vs the previous 10 s) so the post-clear refill transient does not false-positive, and use our own lowered setpoint as stateless memory to raise the threshold while mitigating so restoration cannot trip the detector.

Both are below 10.9 V (margins 0.31 V and 0.36 V), so no healthy sample satisfies the test. THR(tank2 loop, which drives pump1) = 10.5 V: measured fault-free maxima are 8.76 V start-up (range [6.08,8.76], mean 8.27 V) and 9.26 V settled (range [8.52,9.26], mean 8.96 V), both below 10.5 V (margins 1.74 V and 1.24 V). Error ranges do not matter because the effort clause alone already excludes every healthy sample: start-up mean|error| is 0.1262 (max 0.1558) for tank1 and 0.1091 (max 0.1531) for tank2; settled mean|error| is 0.0154 (max 0.0736) and 0.0202 (max 0.0495). While our own mitigation is active (active setpoint < nominal-0.005) the effort clause is raised to 11.6 V, above any restoration transient (worst calculated refill ramp for a 0.005 m step: ~9.7 V on the tank1 loop, ~9.8 V on the tank2 loop) yet still below the 12 V a live leak pins the loop at. proposed_change: 1) Detect faults with absolute loop drive instead of an effort ratio: flag when the 10 s mean pump effort of a tank's own loop (tank1 -> pump2, tank2 -> pump1) reaches 10.9 V / 10.5 V, i.e. clearly above that loop's measured fault-free maximum (10.59 V / 9.26 V) and near the 12 V pump limit that any >=~1.1x outlet leak forces. 2) Suppress the post-clear refill transient with a recovery gate: drop the flag when the 10 s mean level has risen by more than 0.012 m or the 10 s mean error has fallen by more than 0.02 relative to the previous 10 s. 3) Keep the setpoints mostly nominal: lower a tank's setpoint only while it is flagged AND its 10 s mean error still exceeds 0.10 m (i.e. the loop genuinely cannot track, which is exactly the case where the level is pinned and lowering buys IAE), and only down to nominal-0.10 m; restore at 0.005 m per call when the tank is not flagged and its loop drive is relaxed. While mitigating, the detection threshold is raised to 11.6 V (inferred statelessly from active_setpoints < nominal), so our own restoration ramps can never re-trigger a false flag, while a still-live leak keeps the loop at 12 V and stays flagged.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The current detector compares the effort in the SECOND half of the 50-sample window to the effort in the FIRST half (ratio = recent/baseline, ELEVATED_RATIO = 1.8) and only fires if that ratio exceeds 1.8 AND the average |error| over the last 25 s exceeds 0.03. A persistent outlet leak does not produce a brief step: it forces the leaking loop to its 12 V ceiling and then HOLDS it there. Once effort is pinned at 12 V, both halves of the window are sitting at 12 V, so the ratio collapses to ~1.0 and can never reach 1.8 — the detector is structurally blind to the exact fault it is supposed to catch. In the traces the tank1 loop is already at 11.2-12.0 V from t=160 on, and the tank2 loop at 10.4-12.0 V from t=220 on, yet flags stay '-' for the whole leak. The |error|>0.03 gate is also not the problem (errors are 0.2+), it is the ratio gate. Net effect: essentially every leaking second is a missed anomaly (251/249/397/196/202 per tank), which at 300 pts/event dominates the score (388k of the 389k total). There are no violations and no false positives, so the ONLY real defect is missed detection; the setpoint actuator and restore logic are secondary.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Replace the within-window ratio-of-effort test with an ABSOLUTE test on each loop's own pump effort (10 s mean) against a saturation-band threshold (11.0 V of the 12 V ceiling). This is per-tank by construction: because tank1 is fed mainly by pump 2 through tank3 and tank2 mainly by pump 1 through tank4, a leak in one lower tank drives ONLY that tank's own loop to saturation while the other loop is unaffected or slightly reduced. Keep the setpoints at their nominal values (clamped to the allowed band): for a leaking tank the loop is saturated, so lowering its target cannot change the mass-balance-limited level, and if the target ever became reachable the loop would desaturate and destroy the very symptom being detected. Returning nominal also guarantees restore_gap = 0 and cannot regress the no-fault baseline.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The detector compares two halves of the SAME 50-sample window (median of the recent half vs median of the earlier half). A leak makes the leaking tank's own PI loop saturate at the 12 V pump cap, and it stays saturated for the whole fault: once the loop has been pinned for more than ~25 s, both halves of the window contain the same saturated value, so ratio -> 1.0 and the test can never fire. That is exactly what the traces show: tank1_leak holds tank1-loop effort at 12.0 V from t=170 to t=440, both_leaks holds BOTH loops at 12.0 V, yet every call reports flag=[-,-]. Every fault second is therefore a missed anomaly (196-397 per scenario, 300 pts each = the whole 60k-120k score). A secondary defect: the 'calm' test (ratio<1.2 and mean|e|<0.03, both window-relative) is also unreachable, so the setpoint restore path never runs meaningfully. The cross-coupling does not hide the fault - it makes it crisper: a leak in tankN pins the OTHER pump's controller (tank1 leak -> pump2 = tank1 loop effort = 12 V), while the healthy partner loop stays at 8-9 V, so the two loops are cleanly separable by an ABSOLUTE effort threshold anchored on the measured fault-free statistics.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Replace the intra-window ratio test with an absolute, physically-anchored test: (1) the loop effort sits at the pump cap (>=11.4 V for at least 4 of the last 12 samples - healthy loops never exceed 10.59 V / 9.26 V), AND (2) the tank level is not climbing (10-sample level slope <= 0.0018 m/s), which separates a genuine leak (level flat or falling while the pump is pinned) from a post-fault refill (level rising > 0.0025 m/s while the pump is still pinned). Keep setpoint mitigation small and level-referenced so the pump stays saturated and the anomaly signature cannot be erased by our own action.

proposed_change: 1) Detection: per tank, compute cnt = number of the last 12 one-second pump_effort samples >= 11.4 V (pump saturation; healthy maxima are 10.59 V and 9.26 V, pumps cap at 12 V). It is structurally blind to any fault that lasts longer than the window's internal comparison horizon (~25 s). Once a leak persists, BOTH halves of the 50 s window are inside the fault, and worse, the leaking tank's own loop is pinned at the 12 V pump limit, so baseline and recent medians are both ~12 V (or both ~10 V on the ramp) and the ratio collapses to ~1.0. Same for both_leaks (397 combined missed seconds) and the two severe-persistent cases. All 5 fault scenarios score 58k-119k, essentially 100% missed-anomaly cost (300 pts/s), with zero flags ever raised and IAE only ~120. The zero-action setpoint policy also means no restoration behaviour exists at all.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Replace the contaminated within-window ratio with absolute, physically-anchored evidence: a tank is leaking iff (a) its OWN loop effort (off-diagonal pairing: tank1 loop = pump2, tank2 loop = pump1) sits above anything the healthy plant ever produces and (b) its level error is one the loop cannot close and (c) the level is no longer rising. Path (a) alone must be an absolute threshold anchored to the measured healthy envelope (<=10.54 V tank1, <=9.26 V tank2) because a ratio against the window's own past is destroyed by saturation.

proposed_change: Structural rewrite of the detection logic, keeping the same signature. (1) Per tank, take the last 10 samples of the window for loop effort, |level error| and level, and the 10 before that for the level trend. (2) Flag a tank iff its OWN loop is pushed above the healthy envelope (tank1 loop/pump2: 10.70 V; tank2 loop/pump1: 9.80 V) with a level error the loop cannot close (0.085 / 0.075 m), or the loop is essentially saturated (>11.40 V with |e|>0.03), AND in both cases the tank is no longer refilling (level trend <= 0.003 m per 10 samples). (3) The level-trend guard is the discriminator that removes the two legitimate look-alikes: the start-up transient (large error but level rising) and the post-fault wind-up recovery (12 V and large error but level rising at 0.02-0.04 m per 10 s). (4) Setpoint mitigation is now active but small and self-limiting: while a tank is flagged its setpoint drops 0.02 per call, floored at nominal-0.04, and when the flag clears it is stepped back 0.02 per call to nominal, so restore_gap returns to 0 for cleared faults. This is IAE-neutral when the loop is pinned at the voltage limit (the level is set by the 12 V inflow, not by the setpoint) and keeps a large safety margin to the 0.02 m low limit.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The detector's fault *onset* logic is adequate; the damage is done by the level-trend guard being calibrated as 'any positive drift counts as refilling'. During a long leak the tank relaxes asymptotically toward its leak-equilibrium level (h1 ~0.08-0.10 m in both_leaks) while its own off-diagonal loop is pinned on the 12 V rail, so the level creeps up at only ~0.2-0.3 mm/s (0.003 m per 10 samples) — exactly the value the guard used as 'rising'. That silently un-flagged tank1 for t=230-250 s (30 of its 38 missed seconds) in both_leaks and is the single largest block of missed anomalies on the battery. Second, the 10 s-mean error requirement (ERR_HI=0.085) is redundant with the effort condition, because no healthy value can ever reach the effort cut: in tank1_severe_persistent the call at t=410 already had a 10 s mean effort of 10.8 V and a 10 s mean |e| of 0.078 V, so the flag was delayed by a whole extra call (10 s = 300 points) that the 4 s-mean error (0.11) would have caught. Third, the trailing-edge false positives (7-9 s per fault clear) are structural (the call before the clear cannot see it), but they are inflated when the flag is not released by the *first* call after the clear, so the refilling release test must fire on as little as ~1 s of recovery evidence.

Two branches: fast = 4 s mean effort > 10.95 V (tank1) / 10.05 V (tank2) with 4 s mean |e| > 0.035 / 0.030; rail = 10 s mean effort > 11.20 V with 10 s mean |e| > 0.010. failure_analysis.what_failed: Two coupled defects. (1) The level-trend guard is calibrated at the wrong scale: RISE = 0.003 m per 10 samples is below the slow POSITIVE level creep a leaking tank shows in this cross-coupled plant (in both_leaks, tank1 leaking + tank2 also leaking, h1 creeps +3 mm per 10 s because the partner loop's saturated pump1 pushes extra water into tank3 and hence into tank1). The guard therefore declares 'refilling' and switches the flag OFF in the middle of a genuine 200 s tank1 leak: the t=230/240/250 s decisions are flag=[-,Y] while fault=[Y,Y] (30 s booked as missed at 300 pts/s). (2) Detection latency is dominated by the error-amplitude condition, not the effort condition. The leaking loop crosses the saturation band within ~5 s of onset (tank1 effort 11.2 V at t=160, tank2 10.4 V at t=220), but the required |e|>0.085 / >0.075 is only reached 10-20 s later: tank1_severe is missed at t=410 with v=10.8 V and mean|e|=0.078 (just under 0.085) even though the loop is already pinned, and the same holds for the mild tank2 onsets (14 missed s). The ungated setpoint lowering is a third, latent defect: shrinking the setpoint on a tank whose loop is already at the 12 V rail only removes the error the detector needs, so it can un-detect a mild leak.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Keep the mandatory level-trend discriminator (nothing else separates a pinned leak from the post-clear refill), but place its threshold at the refill scale (>=10 mm per 10 s, refills run at 20-45 mm per 10 s while fault creep stays <=7 mm per 10 s). Make the loop effort the fast primary condition (10 s mean >=10.75 V tank1 / >=9.50 V tank2, or 4 s mean >=11.05 V / >=9.80 V) with a small signed-error corroboration (>=0.045 m / >=0.035 m, well under the fault equilibrium error of >=0.076 m that even a 1.5x leak produces once the loop rails). Gate any setpoint reduction on the error being >0.12 m so the detector's own signal is never removed.

proposed_change: Rewrite the per-tank detector as a conjunction of three independent, physically-anchored conditions evaluated on each tank's OWN loop (tank1->pump2, tank2->pump1): (a) effort high - 10 s mean >= V_SLOW[tank] OR 4 s mean >= V_FAST[tank], both placed strictly above the measured healthy envelope maxima (10.59 V / 9.26 V); (b) level not refilling - 10 s mean level rise < 0.010 m (refills after a clear run 20-45 mm per 10 s, fault-time creep is <=7 mm per 10 s); (c) signed setpoint error corroboration - 10 s mean or 4 s mean of (setpoint - level) >= 0.045 m / 0.035 m. Detection speed comes from (a) (rails in ~5 s); (b) stops the loop wind-up after the leak clears from being booked as FP; (c) stops the small error step created by setpoint restoration from being booked as FP. Setpoint policy: while a tank is flagged, lower its setpoint by 0.02 m per call (floor nominal-0.04, clamp [0.05,0.48]) ONLY if the mean error exceeds 0.12 m, so the mitigation can never erase the error signature it depends on; while clean, walk the setpoint back to nominal at 0.02 m per call so the restore gap closes within 2 calls.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The champion's arbitration between 'leak while the loop is pinned' and 'refilling after the leak cleared' is a coarse 10 s mean-drift test (drift > 0.003 m comparing mean(level[-10:]) to mean(level[-20:-10])) combined with effort thresholds that sit only just above the fault-free envelope (EFF_HI 10.70 V for the tank1 loop whose healthy maximum is 10.59 V; 9.80 V for the tank2 loop whose healthy maximum is 9.26 V) gated by |error| (>0.085 / >0.075) and a rail test at 11.40 V. Three consequences: (1) once the supervisor has lowered the setpoint, a genuine leak leaves the level creeping slowly (both_leaks tank1, t=230-250: 0.077->0.087 m, i.e. ~0.0004 m/s = 0.004 m per 10 s) which exceeds the 0.003 m drift gate, so the 'rising' guard silences a real fault for 38 s on tank1 and 14 s on tank2 in both_leaks alone; (2) using the MEAN of the effort over 10 s dilutes the fault-onset ramp with pre-fault samples, so a fault that starts 3-5 s before a call (tank1_severe onset ~403, effort mean at t=410 only 10.8 V) is not booked until the next call - a full 10 s (10 missed events) of pure latency; (3) the effort/error thresholds just above the healthy envelope fire during the wound-up recovery of a cleared fault, producing the 7/5/9/6 false positives and 0-violation but noisy behaviour seen in tank1_leak, tank2_leak and both_leaks. Every one of these is an arbitration/threshold defect, not a missing signal.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Make the primary detector a count of samples of the tank's OWN loop effort sitting on the pump rail inside the last 10 s (>= 11.4 V for both loops, i.e. 0.81 V above the highest fault-free tank1-loop sample 10.59 V and 2.14 V above the highest tank2-loop sample 9.26 V), which is immune to healthy operation and recovers the full call of onset latency that the 10 s mean wastes. Arbitrate leak-vs-recovery with an instantaneous level RATE (mean of the last three 1 s differences, threshold 0.0012 m/s), which is ~3x above the slowest leak creep (0.0004 m/s) and ~2-3x below the post-clear refill rate (0.0025-0.0043 m/s); an absolute 10 s drift threshold cannot separate these two regimes. Keep the setpoint drop small (0.02 per call, max 0.04) so that the loop of a >=1.5x leak still cannot hold the setpoint and stays pinned, and apply the restore steps while the loop is still pinned so that restoring never bumps the effort toward the rail.
failure_analysis.expected_effect: baseline unchanged (no window can reach the rail: healthy max effort 10.59 V < 11.4 V, so flag count is identically zero -> 0 false positives, IAE 61.31); both_leaks tank1 missed 38 -> ~0-5, tank2 14 -> ~5, false positives cut by removing the effort/error thresholds; tank1/tank2 severe persistent onset booked at the first call after the ramp (t=410 instead of t=420).

self_check: TANK1 LOOP (telemetry key tank1.pump_effort = pump 2). Fault-free reference ranges: start-up [4.15, 10.59] V, settled [8.79, 10.54] V. Rail test = at least RAIL_N=2 of the last 10 samples >= 11.4 V. Every healthy sample is <= 10.59 V, i.e. 0.81 V below 11.4 V, so the rail count of any fault-free window is 0 <= 1 -> no flag is possible in baseline_no_fault (matches the measured range with a 0.81 V guard band). For a real leak the loop is pinned at the 12 V pump limit, count ~10 >= 2 -> flags. TANK2 LOOP (tank2.pump_effort = pump 1). Fault-free: start-up [6.08, 8.76] V, settled [8.52, 9.26] V; the highest healthy value 9.26 V is 2.14 V below 11.4 V -> rail count 0 -> no flag. RISE TEST. Suppress only if mean of the last three 1 s level differences > 0.0012 m/s. Healthy start-up rate measured from the trace is ~0.00047-0.0007 m/s (tank1 0.145->0.192 m over 100 s; tank2 0.205->0.211 m over 10 s) and settled healthy rate is <0.0005 m/s, i.e. below 0.0012, but this test can only ever SUPPRESS a flag, it can never create one, so even a healthy start-up cannot false-positive through it. The leak signature it must pass: both_leaks tank1 at t=230-250 creeping at ~0.0004 m/s (0.0004 < 0.0012 -> flag kept, no miss). The signature it must block: post-clear refill at 0.0025-0.0043 m/s (>0.0012 -> flag dropped, no false positive), e.g. tank1 at t=360 rising 0.104->0.146 m in 10 s. Frozen setpoints (0.30/0.35) and the 0.02 step mean the restore action adds at most 0.02*40 = 0.8 V of proportional effort, so it cannot drive a loop to 11.4 V (worst case ~9.3+0.8 = 10.1 V).
proposed_change: Replace the mean-effort/|error|/10 s-drift detector with a two-stage detector per tank. Stage 1 (primary, unambiguous): count how many of the last 10 one-second samples of that tank's OWN loop effort are >= 11.4 V; >= 2 such samples means the loop is sitting on the pump ceiling, something the fault-free plant never does (tank1 loop healthy max 10.59 V, tank2 loop healthy max 9.26 V). This removes the dependence on |error| (which the supervisor's own setpoint lowering shrinks) and removes the 10 s mean dilution that cost a full call of onset latency. Stage 2 (arbitration only): compute the mean of the last three one-second level differences (m/s). If it exceeds 0.0012 m/s the tank is refilling after its fault has physically cleared (measured refill 0.0025-0.0043 m/s) and the flag is dropped; a leak that is already compensated creeps at <=0.0004-0.0013 m/s and keeps its flag. Setpoint policy kept but made collision-free: drop 0.02 per flagged call with a hard floor of nominal-0.04 (keeps tank1 >= 0.26 m and tank2 >= 0.31 m, which is still above the leak-limited equilibrium levels 0.21 m / 0.274 m for a >=1.5x leak, so the loop stays pinned and the level is unaffected), and restore 0.02 per unfaulted call, which happens while the loop is still pinned during the refill, so restoring never pushes the effort up. Diagnosis string carries rail counts and the level rate for traceability. No exceptions possible: pure arithmetic on a >=12 sample window.

failure_analysis.what_failed: Detection latency, not detection logic, dominates the score. A leak always drives its own off-diagonal loop into the 12 V pump ceiling (even a 1.5x leak needs ~15 V), but the old detector demanded 2 samples above 11.4 V, so the first call whose window already contained rail samples was still booked as a miss: tank2 missed 14 (tank2_leak) and 24 (both_leaks) events, i.e. 1.4-2.4 calls late. The extra call in both_leaks is physics: while tank1's pump is pinned at 12 V it pushes 20% of its flow straight into tank2, masking tank2's new leak and slowing its ramp. The refill gate's RISE_FAST=0.0012 m/s also sat *below* the documented leak-creep ceiling (<=0.0013 m/s), so slowly-creeping leaks were silently classified as 'refilling' and suppressed. Residual false positives (5-9/tank) are the 10 s flag hold across a clear plus wound-up-loop windup.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Keep the rail as the mitigation-invariant core, but add a per-tank auxiliary 'effort high + large level deficit + level not falling away' path to recover the onset call, and always re-verify that this path cannot fire inside the recorded fault-free effort/error envelopes before trusting the extra detections.

self_check: RAIL 11.4 V vs fault-free loop-effort maxima: tank1 loop 10.59 V (start-up) / 10.54 V (settled) -> margins 0.81 / 0.86 V; tank2 loop 8.76 V / 9.26 V -> margins 2.64 / 2.14 V, so one rail sample is unambiguous. AUX thresholds 11.0 V (tank1 loop) and 9.9 V (tank2 loop) sit above those same maxima by 0.41/0.46 V and 1.14/0.64 V. AUX error gate 0.05 m: healthy settled error reaches 0.0736 m (tank1) and 0.0495 m (tank2), so the error gate alone is NOT discriminating - it is only ever ANDed with an effort level (>9.9 V) that healthy operation never reaches, and with a non-positive level rate, which healthy settled operation (rising toward setpoint) never shows. Refill gate 0.0018 m/s sits between leak creep (<=0.0013 m/s) and post-clear refill (0.0025-0.0043 m/s), so genuine onsets are no longer gated as 'refilling' while clear-time windup still is. Baseline false-positive risk is therefore zero by construction for tank2 (effort <=9.26 V < 9.9 V) and for tank1 (effort <=10.59 V < 11.0 V).
proposed_change: Replace the 'count >= 2 samples at 11.4 V' test with a single rail sample (RAIL_N=1), raise RISE_FAST to 0.0018 m/s so leak creep is no longer mistaken for refilling, and add a per-tank auxiliary detector (effort max above a per-loop threshold that healthy operation never reaches, a large level deficit, a rising effort, and a non-positive level rate) to catch a leak one call before its loop reaches the rail. Setpoint mitigation and the 0.04 m reduction floor are unchanged, and setpoints ramp back to nominal 0.02 m per call once the flag clears.

One shared 11.40 V rail is applied to both loops although the tank2 loop's fault-free envelope tops out at 9.26 V, so a tank2 leak is only flagged after its own PI has wound all the way to the 12 V ceiling: 1-3 calls late, i.e. 14 missed events in tank2_leak / tank2_severe and 24 in both_leaks (4200-7200 points, the largest single cost). Second, the 1.2 mm/s 'refilling' gate sits inside the leak-creep band (<=1.3 mm/s), so an early-onset leak whose level is still creeping up toward the leak-limited equilibrium is booked as a miss (tank1's 8 misses). Level-rate gate 0.0016 m/s lies between leak creep (<=0.0013 m/s) and post-clear refill (0.0025-0.0043 m/s), a factor 1.6-2.7 separation. Healthy settled |error| ranges are tank1 0.0062-0.0736 and tank2 0.0019-0.0495, so the 0.03 error term would false-fire on its own and the effort rail carries the discrimination; the start-up transient (effort <=10.59/8.76 V, level rising faster than 2 mm/s) stays below every rail and is additionally blocked by the refill gate.
proposed_change: Use per-tank hard and soft effort rails sized from each loop's own fault-free envelope (tank1 11.40/11.05 V, tank2 10.90/10.35 V), counted over the newest 6 samples rather than the last 10 so onset is dated by the most recent evidence, and gate them with a 1.6 m/s level-rate test that separates leak creep from post-clear refill. Snap the mitigated setpoint back to nominal as soon as the tank reaches it, so restoration costs no extra calls.
